claims.content: To transfer reporting responsibility (R^2) for a track by having a C2 JU relinquish or assume R^2 in accordance with the applicable R^2 rules.

goal.raw_text: To transfer reporting responsibility (R^2) for a track by having a C2 JU relinquish or assume R^2 in accordance with the applicable R^2 rules.

claims.content: C2 JU
For air, surface, or land tracks, the C2 JU is capable of assuming R^2 for the track.
For air, surface, or land tracks, the C2 JU has initially achieved Active status or has returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
For air, surface, or land tracks, sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed before transmitting the tracks.
For air and surface tracks, the minimum wait before transmitting tracks is 12 seconds; for land tracks, the minimum wait before transmitting tracks is 48 seconds.

The use case is initiated when a C2 JU receives a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than the local TQ, or receives a remote track report for the track which contains a TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN, for a real-time Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track.

trigger.raw_text: The use case is initiated when a C2 JU receives a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than the local TQ, or receives a remote track report for the track which contains a TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN, for a real-time Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track.

claims.content: C2 JU receives a remote track report for a real-time track.
C2 JU receives a remote track report with TQ greater than the local TQ for a real-time track.
Upon reception of a remote track report with TQ greater than the local TQ, the C2 JU relinquishes R^2 for the real-time track.

After applying all the applicable rules, upon reception of a remote track report with TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose Source TN is greater than the local Source TN, the C2 JU relinquishes R^2 for the real-time track.
A C2 JU with R^2 retains the responsibility until it is relinquished in accordance with the rules or until the track is dropped.

Common tracking shares a common track number and shifts R^2 between C2 JUs; each air, surface (maritime), land (ground), and space tracked object is normally reported by one C2 JU while other C2 JUs withhold their reports.

For air, surface, or land tracks, C2 JUs capable of assuming R^2 shall not transmit tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed; the minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds and for land tracks is 48 seconds.

For Subsurface tracks, it is often desirable that more than one JU report the same Subsurface contact using different TNs; the first JU to report a contact assumes reporting responsibility for that Track Number, and no other JU shall report the contact using that track number unless one of the specified conditions occurs, including receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message containing the TN.

If a locally derived ballistic missile track is uncorrelated with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG, the C2 JU shall report on the uncorrelated local ballistic missile track and shall assume R^2 for that track in accordance with the R^2 rules.

If the received remote track report does not cause relinquishment under the applicable TQ or Source TN rules, the C2 JU with R^2 retains responsibility for the real-time track until it is relinquished in accordance with the rules or until the track is dropped.

If the track is a ballistic missile track, a unit assuming R^2 for the ballistic missile track need not assume R^2 for the associated launch point; the unit no longer holding R^2 on the ballistic missile track may continue to report the launch point in accordance with the transmit/receive rules.

If IFF/SIF surveillance data are involved, the JU with R^2 reports all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for that track in accordance with the transmit rules for the J3 messages; JUs without R^2 monitor such data and only report if they hold different data with the J7.5 message.
If the C2 JU assumes R^2 for a track, the J3.XC1 message is transmitted only by the JU with R^2, at the next opportunity for new tracks when assuming R^2 or when data changes.
For air, surface, or land tracks, the minimum wait before transmitting tracks may be either an automatic or a manual function.
If a C2 JU is deactivating a receive filter, the minimum wait before reporting air, surface, or land tracks also applies.

1. If a C^2 JU capable of assuming R^2 for air, surface, or land tracks has not completed sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration, or the minimum wait has not elapsed (12 seconds for air and surface tracks; 48 seconds for land tracks), the C^2 JU shall not transmit those tracks; Exit: track transmission is deferred until the checks and minimum wait are satisfied.
2. If a J3.7 message is transmitted by a non-R^2 JU with the Response Indicator set to value 1, it shall not affect reporting responsibility; Exit: reporting responsibility remains unchanged.

3. For Subsurface tracks, if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message containing the TN is received, the prohibition on another JU reporting the contact using that track number is lifted; Exit: another JU may report the contact using that track number under the stated drop-track condition.

4. For an emergency point, if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the unit with R^2 is declared inactive, or no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R^2 for the point; Exit: the assuming JU shall use the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit, and the latest JU to report the point has R^2.

5. If a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, or a J2 PPLI message other than J2.0 is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU, a C^2 JU shall assume R^2 of an IU in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C^2 JU has correlated local sensor data; Exit: the C^2 JU assumes R^2 for the IU.
6. If the track is dropped, the JU with R^2 does not retain responsibility beyond the drop; Exit: R^2 retention for that track ends when the track is dropped.

7. If a J3.5 (PTI = 0) message is received, Course and Speed shall be set to No Statement, the Track Quality field shall be set to 0, and Course, Speed, and Track Quality shall not be processed; Exit: those fields from the J3.5 (PTI = 0) message are not processed.
The C2 JU has relinquished R^2 for the real-time track upon reception of a remote track report with TQ greater than the local TQ.

After applying all the above rules, the C2 JU has relinquished R^2 for the real-time track upon reception of a remote track report with TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose Source TN is greater than the local Source TN.

When a locally derived ballistic missile track is uncorrelated with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG, the C2 JU has reported on the uncorrelated local ballistic missile track and has assumed R^2 for that track in accordance with the R^2 rules.
For an emergency point, a JU assuming R^2 shall use the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.
For an emergency point, the latest JU to report the point has R^2.
For Subsurface tracks, the first JU to report a contact assumes reporting responsibility for that Track Number.
